questions.q: The differential equation of the family of circles passing through the origin and having centre at the line \(y=x\) is:
questions.sol:
Circles: \(x^2+y^2-2a(x+y)=0\), so \(2a=\dfrac{x^2+y^2}{x+y}\). Differentiating: \(x+yy'=a(1+y')\).
Substituting \(a\): \(2(x+yy')(x+y)=(x^2+y^2)(1+y')\Rightarrow y'\left(2xy+2y^2-x^2-y^2\right)=x^2+y^2-2x^2-2xy\),
i.e. \(y'(x^2-y^2-2xy)=x^2-y^2+2xy\), which is option (b).

questions.sol:
One parameter, so the order is \(1\). Differentiating: \(2yy'=a\).

Differentiating: \(10f=5f+5xf'-5x^4\Rightarrow xf'-f=x^4\Rightarrow\left(\dfrac fx\right)'=x^2\), so \(f=\dfrac{x^4}{3}+Cx\).
\(x=1\): \(0=5f(1)-10\Rightarrow f(1)=2\Rightarrow C=\dfrac53\). \(f(3)=27+5=32\).

questions.q: Let \(y=y(x)\) be solution of the following differential equation \(e^y\dfrac{dy}{dx}-2e^y\sin x+\sin x\cos^2x=0\), \(y\left(\dfrac\pi2\right)=0\). If \(y(0)=\log_e(\alpha+\beta e^{-2})\), then \(4(\alpha+\beta)\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(u=e^y\): \(u'-2u\sin x=-\sin x\cos^2x\), I.F. \(e^{2\cos x}\): \(u=\tfrac{c^2}2-\tfrac c2+\tfrac14+\tfrac34e^{-2c}\) with \(c=\cos x\). At \(x=0\): \(u=\tfrac14+\tfrac34e^{-2}\).

If \(y=y(x),\ y\in\left[0,\dfrac\pi2\right)\) is the solution of the differential equation \(\sec y\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\sin(x+y)-\sin(x-y)=0\), with \(y(0)=0\), then \(5y'\left(\dfrac\pi2\right)\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(\sec^2y\,dy=2\sin x\,dx\Rightarrow\tan y=2-2\cos x\). At \(\tfrac\pi2\): \(\tan y=2\), \(y'=2\sin x\cos^2y=\tfrac25\).

Let the curve \(y=y(x)\) be the solution of differential equation, \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2(x+1)\). If the numerical value of area bounded by the curve \(y=y(x)\) and \(x\)-axis is \(\dfrac{4\sqrt8}3\), then the value of \(y(1)\) is equal to ______.

Let \(y=y(x)\) be the solution of the differential equation \(x\,dy-y\,dx=\sqrt{(x^2-y^2)}\,dx\), \(x\ge1\), with \(y(1)=0\). If the area bounded by the line \(x=1,\ x=e^\pi,\ y=0\) and \(y=y(x)\) is \(\alpha e^{2\pi}+\beta\), then the value of \(10(\alpha+\beta)\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol: \(y=x\sin(\ln x)\). With \(t=\ln x\): area \(=\int_0^\pi e^{2t}\sin t\,dt=\tfrac{e^{2\pi}+1}5\).

Let \(y=y(x)\) be the solution curve of the differential equation \((1+x^2)\,dy+(y-\tan^{-1}x)\,dx=0\), \(y(0)=1\). Then the value of \(y(1)\) is:
questions.sol:
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{y}{1+x^2}=\dfrac{\tan^{-1}x}{1+x^2}\), I.F. \(=e^{\tan^{-1}x}\). With \(t=\tan^{-1}x\):
\(ye^t=\int te^t\,dt=(t-1)e^t+C\), so \(y=t-1+Ce^{-t}\).
\(y(0)=1\Rightarrow C=2\). Hence \(y(1)=\dfrac{\pi}{4}-1+\dfrac{2}{e^{\pi/4}}\).

questions.q: Let \(y=y(x)\) be the solution of the differential equation \(\sec x\dfrac{dy}{dx}-2y=2+3\sin x\), \(x\in\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\), \(y(0)=-\dfrac74\). Then \(y\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}-2y\cos x=(2+3\sin x)\cos x\); I.F. \(=e^{-2\sin x}\). With \(u=\sin x\):
\[ye^{-2u}=\int(2+3u)e^{-2u}du=-\frac{(2+3u)}{2}e^{-2u}-\frac34e^{-2u}+C.\]
\(y(0)=-1-\tfrac34+C=-\tfrac74\Rightarrow C=0\), so \(y=-\dfrac{2+3\sin x}{2}-\dfrac34\).
\(y\left(\tfrac\pi6\right)=-\tfrac74-\tfrac34=-\tfrac52\).

questions.q: Let the solution curve of the differential equation \(x\,dy-y\,dx=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\,dx\), \(x>0\), \(y(1)=0\), be \(y=y(x)\). Then \(y(3)\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
Put \(y=vx\): \(x^2dv=x\sqrt{1+v^2}\,dx\Rightarrow\dfrac{dv}{\sqrt{1+v^2}}=\dfrac{dx}{x}\Rightarrow\ln\left(v+\sqrt{1+v^2}\right)=\ln x+C\).
\(y(1)=0\Rightarrow C=0\), so \(v+\sqrt{1+v^2}=x\). At \(x=3\): \(\sqrt{1+v^2}=3-v\Rightarrow v=\tfrac43\), so \(y(3)=4\).

questions.q: If \(y=y(x)\) satisfies the differential equation \[16\sqrt{x}\,\sqrt{9+\sqrt x}\,\left(4+\sqrt{9+\sqrt x}\right)\cos y\,dy=(1+2\sin y)\,dx,\quad x>0\] and \(y(256)=\dfrac\pi2\), \(y(49)=\alpha\), then \(2\sin\alpha\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
(The paper prints the first factor as \(\sqrt{x+9\sqrt x}\); the intended factor is \(\sqrt x\sqrt{9+\sqrt x}\).)
Separating: \(\displaystyle\int\frac{16\cos y}{1+2\sin y}dy=\int\frac{dx}{\sqrt x\sqrt{9+\sqrt x}\left(4+\sqrt{9+\sqrt x}\right)}\).
With \(u=4+\sqrt{9+\sqrt x}\), \(du=\dfrac{dx}{4\sqrt x\sqrt{9+\sqrt x}}\): \(8\ln(1+2\sin y)=4\ln u+C\), i.e. \((1+2\sin y)^2=K\left(4+\sqrt{9+\sqrt x}\right)\).
\(x=256\): \(9=9K\Rightarrow K=1\). \(x=49\): \((1+2\sin\alpha)^2=8\Rightarrow2\sin\alpha=2\sqrt2-1\).

Let \(f\) be a twice differentiable non-negative function such that \((f(x))^2=25+\displaystyle\int_0^x\left((f(t))^2+(f'(t))^2\right)dt\). Then the mean of \(f(\log_e1),\,f(\log_e2),\,\dots,\,f(\log_e625)\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
Differentiating: \(2ff'=f^2+f'^2\Rightarrow(f-f')^2=0\Rightarrow f'=f\Rightarrow f=Ce^x\). \(f(0)^2=25\), \(f\ge0\Rightarrow f(x)=5e^x\).
\(f(\log_ek)=5k\); mean of \(5,10,\dots,3125\) is \(5\cdot\dfrac{626}{2}=1565\).

Let a differentiable function \(f\) satisfy the equation \(\displaystyle\int_0^{36}f\left(\frac{tx}{36}\right)dt=4\alpha f(x)\). If \(y=f(x)\) is a standard parabola passing through the points \((2,1)\) and \((-4,\beta)\), then \(\beta^\alpha\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
With \(u=\tfrac{tx}{36}\): \(\dfrac{36}{x}\displaystyle\int_0^xf(u)\,du=4\alpha f(x)\Rightarrow9\int_0^xf=\alpha xf(x)\).
Differentiating: \((9-\alpha)f=\alpha xf'\Rightarrow f=Cx^{(9-\alpha)/\alpha}\). A standard parabola \(y=Cx^2\) needs \(\tfrac{9-\alpha}{\alpha}=2\Rightarrow\alpha=3\).
\((2,1)\Rightarrow C=\tfrac14\), so \(\beta=f(-4)=4\) and \(\beta^\alpha=64\).

Let \(y=y(x)\) be the solution of the differential equation \(x\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\sin2y=x^3(2-x^3)\cos^2y\), \(x\ne0\). If \(y(2)=0\), then \(\tan(y(1))\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
Divide by \(\cos^2y\) and put \(t=\tan y\): \(xt'-2t=2x^3-x^6\), i.e. \(t'-\tfrac2xt=2x^2-x^5\).
I.F. \(=\tfrac1{x^2}\): \(\left(\tfrac{t}{x^2}\right)'=2-x^3\Rightarrow\tfrac{t}{x^2}=2x-\tfrac{x^4}{4}+C\); \(y(2)=0\Rightarrow C=0\).
\(t=2x^3-\tfrac{x^6}{4}\), so \(\tan(y(1))=2-\tfrac14=\tfrac74\).

Let \(y=y(x)\) be the solution of the differential equation \[\frac{dy}{dx}+\left(\frac{6x^2+(3x^2+2x^3+4)e^{-2x}}{(x^3+2)(2+e^{-2x})}\right)y=2+e^{-2x},\] \(x\in(-1,2)\), satisfying \(y(0)=\dfrac32\). If \(y(1)=\alpha(2+e^{-2})\), then \(\alpha\) is equal to:
questions.sol:
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\ln\dfrac{x^3+2}{2+e^{-2x}}=\dfrac{3x^2}{x^3+2}+\dfrac{2e^{-2x}}{2+e^{-2x}}\) equals the coefficient of \(y\), so I.F. \(=\dfrac{x^3+2}{2+e^{-2x}}\).
\(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left[y\cdot\text{I.F.}\right]=x^3+2\Rightarrow y\,\dfrac{x^3+2}{2+e^{-2x}}=\dfrac{x^4}{4}+2x+C\); \(y(0)=\tfrac32\Rightarrow C=1\).
At \(x=1\): \(y\cdot\dfrac{3}{2+e^{-2}}=\dfrac{13}{4}\Rightarrow\alpha=\dfrac{13}{12}\).

questions.q: Let \(f\) be a twice differentiable function such that \(f(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^x\tan(t-x)\,dt-\int_0^xf(t)\tan t\,dt\), \(x\in\left(-\dfrac\pi2,\dfrac\pi2\right)\). Then \(f''\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)+12f'\left(-\dfrac\pi6\right)+f\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)\) is equal to ______.
questions.sol:
\(\int_0^x\tan(t-x)\,dt=\int_{-x}^0\tan u\,du=\ln\cos x\). So \(f=\ln\cos x-\int_0^xf\tan t\,dt\), \(f(0)=0\).
\(f'=-\tan x(1+f)\); with \(g=1+f\): \(g'=-g\tan x\Rightarrow g=\cos x\), so \(f=\cos x-1\).
\(f''\left(\tfrac\pi6\right)=-\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\), \(12f'\left(-\tfrac\pi6\right)=12\cdot\tfrac12=6\), \(f\left(\tfrac\pi6\right)=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}-1\). Sum \(=5\).

questions.q: Let \(y=y(x)\) be the solution of the differential equation \(x\sin\left(\dfrac yx\right)dy=\left(y\sin\left(\dfrac yx\right)-x\right)dx\), \(y(1)=\dfrac\pi2\) and let \(\alpha=\cos\left(\dfrac{y(e^{12})}{e^{12}}\right)\). Then the number of integral values of \(p\), for which the equation \(x^2+y^2-2px+2py+\alpha+2=0\) represents a circle of radius \(r\le6\), is ______.
questions.sol:
With \(y=vx\): \(x^2\sin v\,dv=-x\,dx\Rightarrow\cos v=\ln x+C\); \(y(1)=\tfrac\pi2\Rightarrow C=0\). So \(\alpha=\ln e^{12}=12\).
Circle \(x^2+y^2-2px+2py+14=0\): \(r^2=2p^2-14\), with \(0\(p\in\{\pm3,\pm4,\pm5\}\): \(6\) values.

questions.q: Let \(f:[1,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}\) be a differentiable function defined as \(f(x)=\displaystyle\int_1^xf(t)\,dt+(1-x)(\log_ex-1)+e\). Then the value of \(f(f(1))\) is:
questions.sol:
\(f(1)=e\). Differentiating: \(f'=f-\ln x+\tfrac1x\).
Try \(f=\ln x+g\): \(g'=g\Rightarrow g=Ce^x\); \(f(1)=Ce=e\Rightarrow C=1\). So \(f(x)=\ln x+e^x\).
\(f(f(1))=f(e)=1+e^e\).

questions.q: Let \(y=y(x)\) be the solution of the differential equation \((\tan x)^{1/2}dy=\left(\sec^3x-(\tan x)^{3/2}y\right)dx\), \(0<x<\dfrac\pi2\), \(y\left(\dfrac\pi4\right)=\dfrac{6\sqrt2}{5}\). If \(y\left(\dfrac\pi3\right)=\dfrac45\alpha\), then \(\alpha^4\) equals ______.
questions.sol:
\(\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y\tan x=\dfrac{\sec^3x}{\sqrt{\tan x}}\); I.F. \(=\sec x\): \(y\sec x=\displaystyle\int\frac{\sec^4x}{\sqrt{\tan x}}dx=2t^{1/2}+\frac25t^{5/2}+C\) with \(t=\tan x\).
\(x=\tfrac\pi4\): \(\tfrac{12}{5}=2+\tfrac25+C\Rightarrow C=0\). \(x=\tfrac\pi3\): \(2y=3^{1/4}\left(2+\tfrac65\right)\Rightarrow y=\tfrac85\cdot3^{1/4}\).
\(\alpha=2\cdot3^{1/4}\), \(\alpha^4=48\).

questions.q: Let \(y=y(x)\) be the solution of the differential equation \(\left(x^2-x\sqrt{x^2-1}\right)dy+\left(y\left(x-\sqrt{x^2-1}\right)-x\right)dx=0\), \(x\ge1\). If \(y(1)=1\), then the greatest integer less than \(y(\sqrt5)\) is ______.
questions.sol:
Dividing by \(x-\sqrt{x^2-1}\): \(x\,dy+y\,dx=x\left(x+\sqrt{x^2-1}\right)dx\), so \(xy=\dfrac{x^3}{3}+\dfrac{(x^2-1)^{3/2}}{3}+C\); \(y(1)=1\Rightarrow C=\tfrac23\).
At \(x=\sqrt5\): \(\sqrt5\,y=\dfrac{5\sqrt5}{3}+\dfrac83+\dfrac23\Rightarrow y=\dfrac53+\dfrac{2\sqrt5}{3}\approx3.16\).
Greatest integer less than \(y(\sqrt5)\) is \(3\).
